sentences.text:
The present Writ Petition is filed challenging four notifications bearing Nos.25/2025,
26/2025, 30/2025 and 31/2025, all dated 22.05.2025, as also G.O.Ms.No.487, dated 29.11.2019, issued by the Government of Andhra Pradesh.

2. According to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, a notification is first required to be issued in terms of Section 11 of the Act, 2013, and the said notification is issued whenever the appropriate Government requires any land to be acquired for any public purpose.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
HCJ & RRRJ 3. Section 15 of the Act, 2013, envisages hearing of objections and grants an opportunity to any person interested in any land, which has been notified under sub-section (1) of Section 11 of the Act,
2013, to file objections within a period of sixty days from the date of the publication of the preliminary notification under Section 11 of the Act, 2013.

4. It appears that the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Andhra Pradesh) Rules, 2018, were framed with a view to give effect to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,

sentences.text: 5. According to Rule 6 of the aforementioned Rules, 2018, the District Collector is required to issue a notification in Form-C and may, at any stage of the land acquisition proceedings, invoke the provisions of the Act for settlement of the proceedings by negotiations.

6. In terms of the said provisions of the Rules, 2018, the aforementioned four notifications came to be issued, which provided an opportunity to the interested persons to come forward for settlement by negotiations or file objections within a period of fifteen (15) days from the date of publication of the said notifications.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the period of fifteen days prescribed in terms of the aforementioned notifications runs contrary to Section 15 of the Act, 2013, which otherwise prescribed the period of sixty days.
HCJ & RRRJ 8.

With a view to support and buttress the period of fifteen days as was prescribed in the aforementioned four notifications, it appears that the Government brought about an amendment by virtue of G.O.Ms.No.487, dated 29.11.2019, whereby the existing Form-C which prescribed the period of 'Sixty Days' would be substituted by the words 'Fifteen Days'.
9.

It is in the backdrop of the aforementioned facts, Mr. K. S. Murthy, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners, would submit that the entire procedure adopted by the respondents is bad and unsustainable.

10. Mrs. S. Pranathi, learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents, however,
states that it is only on account of negotiations between willing parties that the proceedings impugned have been issued and in case any land owner including the petitioners do not give consent, then acquisition proceedings by issuing a notification in terms of Section 11 of the Act,
2013, would be commenced.
11.

It is also fairly stated by learned counsel for the respondents that the word 'Objections' used in the amended Form-C would have been more appropriately worded if the same had reflected the word 'Consent'.
12.

In any case, it is stated that the absence of consent from the petitioners and similarly situate others who had not responded to the notifications impugned would not be treated as consent on their part and even in their cases, regular acquisition proceedings by issuance of notification under Section 11(1) of the Act, 2013, would be initiated.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners has no objection to the statement made by learned counsel for the respondents.
14. In that view of the matter, we dispose of this petition.
We make it clear that all issues which were otherwise raised in the present petition with regard to the validity of the impugned provisions and the notifications shall remain open.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.

DHIRAJ SINGH THAKUR, CJ R RAGHUNANDAN RAO, J kbs HCJ & RRRJ HON'BLE MR.
